1. Immune-related oral mucositis/gingival inflammation from pembrolizumab (oral IRAE) — timing (6 months on PD‑1 inhibitor) and localized gum pain/bleeding make this most likely.
2. Radiation-induced mucositis/gingivitis — plausible if radiation involved the head/neck/oral cavity.
3. Plaque-induced gingivitis/periodontitis (bacterial) — common cause of gum pain/bleeding and can occur independently of systemic tests.
4. Medication-related bleeding/gingival change (antiplatelet/anticoagulant, NSAIDs, or drug-induced gingival hyperplasia) — platelet count normal but anticoagulants or local drug effects could explain bleeding.
5. Primary hemostatic disorder (platelet dysfunction or von Willebrand disease) or early hematologic abnormality not detected on routine CBC — less likely given normal platelet count/smear but still possible.

Recommendations (brief): confirm radiation field/timing, obtain medication list, perform oral exam by dentist/ENT (photo of gums), periodontal evaluation, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), platelet function testing or vWF panel if bleeding persists, and consider biopsy of gingiva or referral to oncology/dental specialist for suspected immune-related oral toxicity.
